title: Chemical Systems and Equilibrium
seo_title: Grade 12 Chemistry (SCH4U): Chemical Systems and Equilibrium Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Dynamic equilibrium; Le Châtelier's principle; the equilibrium constant K and ICE tables; acids and bases (Brønsted–Lowry, K<sub>a</sub>, pH and pOH); buffers; and solubility equilibria and K<sub>sp</sub>. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 11 and 12: Science (2008), Chemistry, Grade 12, University Preparation (SCH4U), Strand E: Chemical Systems and Equilibrium)
meta_desc: Free Grade 12 Chemistry (SCH4U) worksheets on chemical equilibrium: dynamic equilibrium, Le Châtelier's principle, equilibrium constants, ICE tables, pH and Ka, buffers and Ksp. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: At equilibrium the forward and reverse rates are equal.
key_sub: Le Châtelier: a system shifts to reduce a change.
body_html:
How to think about it

At equilibrium, reactants and products both remain and their concentrations stay constant. For aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD, K = [C]c[D]d ÷ ([A]a[B]b) (solids and liquids are left out). Use an ICE table (initial, change, equilibrium) to find unknown concentrations.

Adding a reactant, removing a product or changing pressure or temperature shifts the position; only temperature changes K. pH = −log[H₃O⁺] and pH + pOH = 14 at 25 °C. A weak acid has a small Ka. A buffer (a weak acid and its conjugate base) resists pH change.

Example

[H₃O⁺] = 1.0 × 10⁻³ mol/L. pH?

pH = −log(1.0 × 10⁻³)

Answer: 3.0

Example

N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ is exothermic. The temperature is raised. Which way does it shift?

Heat is a product; adding it shifts away from it.

Answer: to the left (less NH₃)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the reaction stops at equilibrium.
  • Putting solids or pure liquids in the K expression.
  • Saying a catalyst shifts the equilibrium: it only gets there faster.

faq.q: What does a large K mean?
faq.a: At equilibrium there are mostly products.
What is left when an acid gives away a proton, such as Cl⁻ from HCl.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium PCl<sub>5</sub> ⇌ PCl<sub>3</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the left
no change in the position of equilibrium
the equilibrium shifts to the right
items.e: There are 1 moles of gas on the left and 2 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: In making ammonia (Haber process): N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −92 kJ. More N<sub>2</sub> is added. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: An engineer wants more H<sub>2</sub> from making hydrogen: CO + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = −41 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of H<sub>2</sub> at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: the energy change = −41 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favors the exothermic direction.

items.q: In a sealed tube of hydrogen and iodine: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI, the energy change = −9 kJ. A catalyst is added. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: A catalyst speeds up both directions equally, so it does not shift equilibrium.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium CO + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right
the equilibrium shifts to the left
no change in the position of equilibrium
items.e: There are the same number of moles of gas on each side.

items.q: An engineer wants more CH<sub>3</sub>OH from making methanol: CO + 2H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ CH<sub>3</sub>OH, the energy change = −91 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of CH<sub>3</sub>OH at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
items.e: Left: 3 mol gas, right: 1 mol gas. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles; lower pressure favors more.

items.q: In making methanol: CO + 2H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ CH<sub>3</sub>OH, the energy change = −91 kJ. Some H<sub>2</sub> is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: In making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, the energy change = −198 kJ. Some SO<sub>3</sub> is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: In making hydrogen: CO + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO<sub>2</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = −41 kJ. Some H<sub>2</sub> is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: In a sealed tube of hydrogen and iodine: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI, the energy change = −9 kJ. The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller). How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: Both sides have 2 mol of gas, so pressure has no effect.

items.q: An engineer wants more NO<sub>2</sub> from a brown gas mixture: N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = +57 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of NO<sub>2</sub> at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
items.e: Left: 1 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles; lower pressure favors more.

items.q: What happens to the equilibrium CH<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO + 3H<sub>2</sub> (all gases) if the pressure is increased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the left
no change in the position of equilibrium
the equilibrium shifts to the right
items.e: There are 2 moles of gas on the left and 4 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles.

items.q: An engineer wants more NO from a hot car engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NO, the energy change = +181 kJ. Which single change increases the amount of NO at equilibrium?
c: The pressure is increased (the container is made smaller).
The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger).
items.e: the energy change = +181 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Heating favors the endothermic direction.

items.q: In a sealed tube of hydrogen and iodine: H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI, the energy change = −9 kJ. More H<sub>2</sub> is added. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: For PCl<sub>5</sub> ⇌ PCl<sub>3</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = 88 kJ mol⁻¹. What happens if the temperature is decreased?
c: the equilibrium shifts to the right and K<sub>c</sub> increases
the equilibrium shifts to the left and K<sub>c</sub> decreases
the equilibrium shifts to the right but K<sub>c</sub> stays the same
items.e: The forward reaction is endothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction. Only temperature changes K<sub>c</sub>.

items.q: For CH<sub>4</sub> + H<sub>2</sub>O ⇌ CO + 3H<sub>2</sub>, the energy change = 206 kJ mol⁻¹. What happens if the temperature is decreased?

the equilibrium shifts to the left and K<sub>c</sub> decreases
the equilibrium shifts to the right but K<sub>c</sub> stays the same
items.e: The forward reaction is endothermic. Cooling favours the exothermic direction. Only temperature changes K<sub>c</sub>.

items.q: In a hot car engine: N<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NO, the energy change = +181 kJ. The temperature is lowered. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: the energy change = +181 kJ, so the forward reaction is endothermic. Cooling favors the exothermic direction.

items.e: Kc = products ÷ reactants with powers = 25.6 mol⁻² L².

items.e: Products over reactants, each concentration raised to the power of its coefficient.

items.q: 2.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 1.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2.0 L. At equilibrium 0.60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 1.4, alcohol 0.40, ester 0.60, water 0.60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0.60² ÷ (1.4 × 0.40) = 0.643.

items.q: At equilibrium for H<sub>2</sub> + I<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2HI: [H<sub>2</sub>] = 0.40, [I<sub>2</sub>] = 0.50, [HI] = 0.80 mol/L. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: Kc = products ÷ reactants with powers = 3.20.

items.q: 5.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5.0 L. At equilibrium 1.5 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3.5, alcohol 1.5, ester 1.5, water 1.5 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1.5² ÷ (3.5 × 1.5) = 0.429.

items.q: For N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g), K<sub>c</sub> = 2.00 at 700 K. What is K<sub>p</sub>? (R = 0.0831 L bar K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
items.e: Kp = Kc(RT)Δn with Δn = −2, so Kp = 5.91 × 10−4.

items.q: At equilibrium for N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub> ⇌ 2NO<sub>2</sub>: [N<sub>2</sub>O<sub>4</sub>] = 0.10, [NO<sub>2</sub>] = 2.0 mol/L. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.

items.q: For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, K = 1.40. What is K for the reverse reaction 2NH₃ ⇌ N₂ + 3H₂?

items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3.2, alcohol 2.2, ester 0.80, water 0.80 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0.80² ÷ (3.2 × 2.2) = 0.0909.

items.q: 2.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5.0 L. At equilibrium 1.5 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 0.50, alcohol 0.50, ester 1.5, water 1.5 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1.5² ÷ (0.50 × 0.50) = 9.00.

items.q: 2.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 4.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 1.0 L. At equilibrium 0.50 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.

items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3.8, alcohol 3.8, ester 1.2, water 1.2 mol. V cancels: Kc = 1.2² ÷ (3.8 × 3.8) = 0.0997.

items.q: 4.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 3.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 5.0 L. At equilibrium 0.50 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.

items.q: 4.0 mol of ethanoic acid and 2.0 mol of ethanol are mixed in 2.0 L. At equilibrium 0.60 mol of ethyl ethanoate has formed: CH₃COOH + C₂H₅OH ⇌ CH₃COOC₂H₅ + H₂O. Calculate K<sub>c</sub>.
items.e: At equilibrium: acid 3.4, alcohol 1.4, ester 0.60, water 0.60 mol. V cancels: Kc = 0.60² ÷ (3.4 × 1.4) = 0.0756.
